Every field of every band, the editorial description / interpretation / pitfalls / references included, is hashed into bands_cid, so editing any of them moves the CID. bands.description: Tessera annual foundation embedding (128-D, stored upstream as int8 + per-pixel f32 scale; recall decodes to f32 for cosine scoring). A learned multimodal vector that fuses Sentinel-2 optical, Sentinel-1 radar, and seasonality into one position-stable vector per cell per year. The default similarity surface for `/v1/find_similar` because it captures land-cover, structure, and recent change in one shot.
bands.interpretation: Compare via cosine similarity (or Hamming on the `geotessera.bin128` sign-bit sibling). Two cells with similarity > 0.85 are usually the same physical archetype (e.g. dense urban, mature mangrove, sparse savanna). Not directly interpretable per dimension — treat as opaque.

bands.pitfalls: Yearly cadence: a cell that flips from forest to clearing mid-year reads as the *annual mean* until the next vintage. Use `temporal_diff` or `phenology` to detect intra-year change.

AOD-550 is column-integrated aerosol optical depth at 550 nm; values >0.4 indicate hazy conditions, >1.0 indicate dust storm or wildfire smoke. SO2 and CO are useful for pinpoint industrial / biomass burning sources.

bands.description: Clay Foundation Model v1.5 per-cell foundation embedding (Made With Clay, Apache-2.0). The cell's 10-band 256×256 Sentinel-2 L2A chip (blue, green, red, rededge1, rededge2, rededge3, nir, nir08, swir16, swir22 in metadata.yaml order, 10 m equivalent) is encoded by a wavelength-conditioned ViT-L/8 MAE; the materializer signs the encoder's last-block CLS token (1024-D, post-norm) as the fact value alongside the temporal+spatial conditioning vectors (sin/cos week-of-year + lat/lng). The cube slot allocates 384 dims at offset 199 as the layout reservation; fact `value` carries the full 1024-D vector and downstream similarity reads that directly. Carved out of the historic `_reserved_512` slot — `_reserved_128` (121 dims at offset 583) is what's left of that slack.
bands.interpretation: Compare via cosine similarity. Two cells with cosine > 0.85 share a 2.56 km × 2.56 km chip-archetype (urban core, mangrove, irrigated cropland, etc.). Wavelength-conditioned: the same encoder produces different embeddings for S2 vs Landsat vs NAIP vs MODIS chips, so always cite the platform tag alongside the model_cid.

bands.pitfalls: Receptive field is 2.56 km × 2.56 km at 10 m pixel pitch — finer than Prithvi (6.7 km) but coarser than Tessera per-pixel (10 m). For sub-chip discrimination chain to `geotessera`. bands.description: Three optical-index scalars derived from Sentinel-2 L2A: NDVI, NDRE, NDMI. The most-pulled vegetation surface — these are what algorithms like `flood_risk@2`, `crop_stress@1`, and `irrigation_demand@1` compose.

dimensions.description: Normalised Difference Vegetation Index
dimensions.formula: NDVI = (B08 − B04) / (B08 + B04), each band first scaled to reflectance as DN * 1e-4 in f64, applied per band before the ratio. Folding the scaling through the ratio is algebraically equal but can differ in the last bits.
dimensions.name: ndvi

dimensions.description: Normalised Difference Red-Edge — chlorophyll-sensitive, less prone to saturation than NDVI
dimensions.formula: NDRE = (B08 − B05) / (B08 + B05), each band first scaled to reflectance as DN * 1e-4 in f64, applied per band before the ratio. Folding the scaling through the ratio is algebraically equal but can differ in the last bits.
dimensions.name: ndre

dimensions.description: Normalised Difference Moisture Index — canopy water content
dimensions.formula: NDMI = (B08 − B11) / (B08 + B11), each band first scaled to reflectance as DN * 1e-4 in f64, applied per band before the ratio. Folding the scaling through the ratio is algebraically equal but can differ in the last bits.
dimensions.name: ndmi

bands.interpretation: NDVI < 0 = water / snow; 0 – 0.2 = bare soil / urban; 0.2 – 0.5 = sparse / stressed vegetation; 0.5 – 0.8 = healthy crops / shrub; > 0.8 = dense closed canopy. NDMI tracks canopy water content (negative = dry, positive = moist). NDRE is more sensitive to chlorophyll than NDVI and saturates later — preferred for in-season nitrogen monitoring.

bands.pitfalls: Read `surface_class` on the fact before the value. It carries the per-pixel Sentinel-2 SCL class the responder actually probed at this cell (`scl`, `label`, `vegetation_valid`) and answers a question `confidence` does not: confidence scores radiometric cleanliness, so a snow-covered field in January is a clean pixel and scores 0.95 while the NDVI on it measures snow, not vegetation. `vegetation_valid: false` (snow, water, shadow) means the number is real but is not a vegetation reading. Prefer this over the scene-level `weather.cloud_cover` / `cloud_pct` proxies: those describe the whole scene, `surface_class` describes this pixel. Absent when the SCL band could not be read, in which case confidence falls back to scene-level cloud cover and the scene-level proxies are all there is. NDVI saturates above ~0.85 (use NDRE / `geotessera` for dense canopies).
bands.references: Tucker 1979 (NDVI); Gitelson & Merzlyak 1994 (NDRE); Gao 1996 (NDMI / NDWI); Xu 2006 (MNDWI = (B03-B11)/(B03+B11)); Key & Benson 2006 (NBR = (B08-B12)/(B08+B12)); Hall et al. 1995 (NDSI = (B03-B11)/(B03+B11)); Zha et al. 2003 (NDBI = (B11-B08)/(B11+B08)); Rikimaru et al. 2002 (BSI = ((B11+B04)-(B08+B02))/((B11+B04)+(B08+B02))); Hardisky et al. 1983 (NDWI_Gao = (B03-B08)/(B03+B08), the leaf-water-content form used by the algal-bloom water gate)

bands.description: IBM-NASA Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL per-cell foundation embedding. The cell's 6-band 224×224 Sentinel-2 L2A chip (Blue/Green/Red/Narrow-NIR/SWIR1/SWIR2 in HLS V2 order, ~30 m equivalent) is encoded by the Vision Transformer; the materializer signs the encoder's last-block CLS token (1024-D, post-norm) as the fact value alongside the temporal-encoder's year + DOY embeddings. The cube slot allocates 384 dims at offset 894 as the layout reservation; fact `value` carries the full 1024-D vector and downstream similarity (find_similar) reads that directly.
bands.interpretation: Compare via cosine similarity. Two cells with cosine > 0.85 share a structural archetype at the 6.7 km × 6.7 km Prithvi receptive-field scale (urban core, tropical forest, irrigated cropland, mangrove, etc.). Scene-aware and date-aware: the temporal encoder shifts the embedding with year + DOY, so two vintages of the same cell are deliberately distinct.

bands.pitfalls: Receptive field is 6720 m × 6720 m at 30 m pixel pitch — the embedding represents a chip centred on the cell, not the 9.55 m cell footprint. Privacy class is `l2_only_with_model_cid` because the embedding can leak chip content; every fact carries the model checkpoint hash so agents can verify the encoder version.

bands.description: Annual nightlight composite at the cell (DMSP-OLS V4 intercalibrated stable lights, 1992-2013). VIIRS DNB v22 was the originally-targeted source but EOG/CSM moved its archive behind OAuth in 2024-2025; the wired open-data path is NOAA NCEI NGDC, the only globally-mirrored, anonymous, Range-readable annual nightlight time series.
bands.interpretation: Strong proxy for human activity intensity at night — picks up settlements down to ~hamlet scale. A drop year-over-year often signals out-migration, conflict, or grid failure; a spike signals new development. Comparing DMSP-OLS DN to VIIRS DNB radiance requires the Li & Zhou 2017 (Remote Sensing 9:637) intercalibration regression — DN is not the same physical unit as nW · cm⁻² · sr⁻¹.

bands.description: Global Multi-Resolution Topography (GMRT) v4.4.1 — global topo-bathymetric surface in metres relative to mean sea level. Produced by the Marine Geoscience Data System (MGDS) at Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory by fusing ship-borne multibeam swaths (~50–100 m native), regional compilations (CCOM, IBCAO, GEBCO), and SRTM30_PLUS into a single seamless quad-tree pyramid. Sign convention: positive = above sea level (topography), negative = below sea level (bathymetry). Anonymous PointServer / GridServer access; no API key.

dimensions.description: Mean of GMRT topo-bathymetric elevation over the cell footprint (single pixel for PointServer, small-bbox mean for GridServer). Positive = above MSL, negative = below MSL.
dimensions.name: topobathy_mean

dimensions.name: topobathy_min

dimensions.description: Maximum elevation over the GridServer-returned pixels covering the cell. Collapses to the same value as the mean when GMRT returns a single pixel.
dimensions.name: topobathy_max

dimensions.description: Population standard deviation of elevation over the GridServer-returned pixels. Returns 0.0 when GMRT returns a single pixel; otherwise serves as a per-cell terrain-roughness proxy.
dimensions.name: topobathy_std

bands.interpretation: `gmrt.topobathy_mean` is the single-pixel reading (PointServer) or small-bbox spatial mean (GridServer over a ~9.55 m cell64 footprint) at the cell. Pair with `gmrt.topobathy_min` / `gmrt.topobathy_max` to bound the cell's vertical extent and `gmrt.topobathy_std` for terrain roughness. Wave_solve and coastal_proximity read the mean as the depth h in the shallow-water solver; flood_risk@2 cross-checks it against Cop-DEM (|cop − gmrt| ≤ 5 m → dem_agreement = 1).

bands.pitfalls: GMRT auto-selects pyramid resolution by bbox extent: cell64-sized requests often return a single pixel in remote basins where the underlying source is SRTM30_PLUS (~1 km) but multiple pixels where multibeam coverage is dense. The reductions therefore reflect the source resolution, not the request bbox — `n_px = 1` in the GmrtWindowSample is the honest signal that the upstream pyramid level is coarser than the cell. Coverage is global (±90° lat × ±180° lng) with no envelope gap, but bathymetric accuracy degrades from ~50 m horizontal in surveyed basins to ~1 km in remote ocean interior.

bands.description: NASA Harvest Galileo per-cell foundation embedding (Base = 768-D / Tiny = 192-D, variant chosen at the sidecar via `EMEM_GALILEO_VARIANT`). The cell's 10-band 8×8 Sentinel-2 L2A chip (B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, B8A, B11, B12 in canonical Galileo `S2_BANDS` order, 30 m equivalent — ~240 m × 240 m physical extent) is encoded by the multi-modal Galileo transformer with the other modalities zero-masked; the materializer signs the encoder's average-pooled token embedding (768-D Base / 192-D Tiny) as the fact value alongside lat/lng + month-of-year conditioning. The cube slot allocates 48 dims at offset 1701 as a compact carrier; the full fact `value` carries the variant-native dim and downstream similarity reads that directly. NOTE: the 48-dim cube slot is only the leading prefix of the 768-D (Base) / 192-D (Tiny) vector — it is a layout reservation, NOT a discriminative reduction (no PCA/learned projection), so the cube slot alone is non-discriminative; the full embedding lives in the fact `value` / cube assembly `extras[]` and that is what cosine/find_similar must read. Carved out of the historic 91-dim `reserved` tail in 2026-05; subsequent reserved offsets stay byte-stable.
bands.interpretation: Compare via cosine similarity. Two cells with cosine > 0.85 share the small-footprint (~240 m × 240 m) chip archetype Galileo learned over global multi-modal corpora. Variant-agnostic: a deployment swapping `EMEM_GALILEO_VARIANT` from Base to Tiny does NOT change the band key — agents see the same `galileo` band, just at a different dim. Always cite the model_cid (Galileo Base = blake2b of nano_galileo_base.pt; Tiny = blake2b of nano_galileo_tiny.pt) so a verifier can pin which encoder version produced the embedding.

materializer.note: retired on this deployment: facts it signed before still read and verify; nothing new materialises

bands.pitfalls: Receptive field is only 240 m × 240 m — much narrower than Prithvi (6.7 km) or Clay (2.56 km). For continental-scale similarity prefer `clay_v1`; for sub-cell discrimination prefer `geotessera` per-pixel. S2-only mode here — Galileo's other modalities (SAR, climate, DEM) are zero-masked at this responder, which biases the embedding toward the optical-only manifold. Privacy class is `public` because the small 8×8 chip is too coarse to leak identifiable scene content.
bands.references: Tseng, G. et al. 2025. Galileo: Learning Global & Local Features of Many Remote Sensing Modalities. https://nasaharvest.github.io/galileo.html ; https://huggingface.co/nasaharvest/galileo ; https://github.com/nasaharvest/galileo
